checkpoint_content_verification.purpose: Opus's audit, 2026-08-27: a sha256 only proves the file wasn't corrupted in transit, not that its content satisfies the claimed DA-V2-init/zero-temporal properties. Re-runnable content check performed on crispwork.
checkpoint_content_verification.note: Only proj_out (the final projection inside each TemporalModule's temporal_transformer, zeroed via motion_module.py's zero_module()) is required to be exactly zero -- that alone makes the residual output = hidden_states + residual collapse to residual regardless of everything upstream. The rest of each motion_module (attention, feedforward, positional encoding) has its own real (nonzero) random init, by design -- an earlier version of this check incorrectly asserted the WHOLE motion_modules subtree must be zero and reported FAIL; corrected to check only proj_out, which is the actual invariant the zero-init claim depends on.

comparability_caveat: This DA-V2-init baseline's KITTI AbsRel (0.1237) is numerically BETTER than the paper's DAv2-L figure (0.137, Table 2) despite DA-V2-S being the smaller model. This is NOT evidence DA-V2-S beats DAv2-L -- the two numbers are not comparable: this run scores only the 13 KITTI clips/manifest present on crispwork (from BENCH-01d's own subset, not the paper's full KITTI population) through this script's own alignment/crop path, while the paper's DAv2-L figure comes from their own full-population single-image protocol (Table 2, not the video Table 1). Do not quote these two numbers side by side as a model comparison.
